name: pdk-baserow-webhook-ordered-recovery
instr:
Table webhooks currently publish after commit into Redis and queue conflicting calls there. During a broker outage a successful row write can fail its HTTP request or lose its webhook; a killed worker can strand a webhook, and retries can arrive behind newer updates. Make REST row create, update and delete webhooks durable and ordered per active webhook across API and worker replicas. Each committed change must reach that webhook with its existing event type and payload (including `webhook_id` and `event_id`), a `sequence` number in the payload starting at 1 for each webhook and increasing by 1 for each subsequent event, and an `X-Baserow-Delivery` header equal to the payload's `event_id` and stable across retry attempts. One row event sent to multiple webhooks must retain the same `event_id` in each webhook's payload, while each webhook has its own sequence stream. REST row create, update and delete must deliver `rows.created`, `rows.updated` and `rows.deleted`, respectively. Keep the existing webhook API fields, call history and test-call endpoint.

A Redis outage of 20 seconds must not prevent REST row writes from returning 2xx; deliver retained events in commit order within 30 seconds after Redis returns, without another row write. A worker killed while a receiver holds the first of ten pending calls must not strand them: resume all ten in order within 45 seconds of replacing the worker, retaining the first delivery id.
